articles.title: Rainbow Warriors overcome scary moment to break through for first win
articles.summary: With the Hawaii football team needing a big play, it was “Tama Time.” Tama Uiliata, lining up as the wildcat, threw the dagger scoring pass to seal the Rainb...
articles.body:
With the Hawaii football team needing a big play, it was "Tama Time."

Tama Uiliata , lining up as the wildcat, threw the dagger scoring pass to seal the Rainbow Warriors ' 29-19 victory over New Mexico State at the Ching Complex on Saturday night.

"That kid is a dynamic player," UH offensive coordinator Anthony Arceneaux said of Uiliata, who usually plays slotback. "That play that we scored was a play (offensive assistant) Coach Winterhawk (Leighton) came up with. We made it our own. (Quarterback) Micah (Alejado) actually called the play. Shoot, after that, it was Tama Time."

A crowd of 11,807 saw Sean Olvera-Harle connect on three field goals, DeVon Rice score two touchdowns, and Alejado rebound from a knockdown hit to help the Warriors win for the first time in 2026 after opening with consecutive losses. The Warriors improved to 12-1 in the inter-conference series, including 8-0 on Oahu.

The Warriors were missing key players on both sides of the ball. Slotback Pofele Ashlock has not played this season while recovering from a leg ailment. Running back Cam Barfield has missed the past 11 quarters because of an ankle injury. Defensive end Lester Lagafuaina also was sidelined because of a shoulder issue. And left guard Lipe Moala was in concussion protocol and not available.

But the Warriors proved to be resilient.

In a scary moment for the Warriors in the third quarter, Alejado was hit by Gabe Peterson , a 6-foot-2, 255-pound hybrid end, and lost the ball. As Alejado was on the turf in a dazed heap, De'Marcus Peters scooped the loose ball and raced 84 yards for the touchdown to tie it at 19-all with 13:15 left in the third quarter. Ilya Uvaydov missed the point-after kick.

But Alejado returned for the ensuing possession and led an 11-play drive that resulted in Olvera-Harle's 33-yard field goal for a 22-19 lead with 8:46 left in the third quarter.

"Hat's off to 12 (Alejado)," Uiliata said. "He's a ballplayer. He went down. but he got back up."

In the fourth quarter, the Aggies failed to convert on a fourth-and-1 play. The Warriors drove to the 6 but were stopped for a 1-yard loss on a third-down run. The Warriors headed toward the sideline, then sprinted to the line of scrimmage. The Aggies, who were not set to defend the fourth-down play, called timeout.

The Warriors then moved Alejado to the slot as Uiliata took the snap. Uiliata rolled to his right, then lofted the 7-yard scoring pass to tight end Frank Abreu in the end zone for a 10-point advantage.

"Micah actually called the play," Uiliata said. "That's trust. That goes a long way, having (Alejado) and Coach (Timmy) Chang trusting me to go back to the basics and play ball."

In the previous week's loss to UNLV, Uiliata did not catch a pass in two targets. On Saturday, he came up with 10 receptions for 107 yards.

"Just going back to the basics and having the coaches believe in me," Uiliata said. "Just having more minutes in the game helped me get back that groove."

Last week, Alejado came out twice for a play apiece against UNLV. This past Tuesday, Alejado was held out of contact drills. After being rocked by Peterson, Alejado was admittedly sore, particularly on his right side. But he rebounded to finish 33-for-45 for 346 yards.

"There are guys who are gamers and rise to the occasion," Arceneaux said of Alejado. "He's one of them."

Alejado and Audric Harris collaborated on four completions for 105 yards. With the Warriors struggling for consistency with the outside receivers, Harris moved from slotback to wideout this week.

For the second consecutive game, Rice started in place of Barfield. Rice scored two first-half touhdowns, finishing the latter with a somersault over an Aggies defender.

Fredia Rice said her son had mastered back flips in high school. "This was the first time he did a somersault," she said smiling.

The Warriors did not force a turnover in the first two games. But they came up with four on Saturday, including two in the second half. They also had a key fourth-down stop.

"It was an emphasis to get around the ball," nickelback Elijah Palmer said. "A couple got called back in previous games. At the end of the day, it was a great feeling to have guys all around."

It was the Warriors' defense that jump-started the scoring in the first quarter.

Mike linebacker Wynden Ho'ohuli punched the ball free from NMSU quarterback Trey Hedden on a scramble. Dime linebacker Jamih Otis recovered at the UH. 36. On the eighth play of the UH drive, Rice took the handoff and outraced two defenders around the right end for his third touchdown of the season.

Olvera-Harle's point-after kick was wide left.

On UH's ensuing possession, Alejado and Harris teamed on a 55-yard, catch-and-dash play to set up Olvera-Harle's 32-yard field goal for a 9-0 lead with 4:28 left in first quarter.

In the second quarter, Alejado and Harris collaborated on a 33-yard play to the NMSU 18. Two plays later, Rice scored his second TD of the half.

articles.title: F1 leader Antonelli wins Spanish Grand Prix as unlucky Norris misses out
articles.summary: The 20-year-old Italian has extended his championship lead to 81 points after 14 rounds.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli has moved a mighty step closer to the Formula One title after winning the first Spanish Grand Prix held at Madrid’s new circuit with a slice of luck on the side.

The 20-year-old Italian’s Madrid victory on Sunday – his eighth win of the season – stretched his championship lead to 81 points after 14 rounds.

Antonelli benefited from a well-timed virtual safety car (VSC) and a calamitous McLaren pit stop on lap 16 of 57 that robbed pole-sitter and early leader Lando Norris of a likely win on a track where overtaking proved almost impossible.

“I think today it’s good to win, but it doesn’t feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win, but overall, we take it,” said Antonelli.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was second, with Norris third. Antonelli now has 292 points compared to his closest rival and teammate George Russell, who finished fifth, on 211.

“There was nothing I could do… just luck not on our side,” said Norris. “I felt like we deserved it today, but that’s racing sometimes.

“I feel like I drove a perfect race today, just luck wasn’t with me.”

Antonelli twice had to give the lead back to Norris on the opening lap after going off and gaining an advantage in a battle through the opening corners. But the Briton then settled into a rhythm and began to pull away.

Verstappen also gained a place that he had to hand back to Antonelli and lost and gained position to Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who then suffered a brake problem that eventually forced the seven-time world champion to retire.

Norris was more than six seconds clear with everything seemingly under control when Aston Martin’s Lance Stroll triggered the VSC by stopping on track on lap 14.

Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell all came in for a cheap pit stop, but Norris was unable to do so, having already gone past the entry point, and by the time he came around again, the VSC had ended.

McLaren called him in anyway on lap 16 for a switch to hard tyres, but he was stopped for seven seconds and returned to the track technically in fifth place, but effectively fourth with new leader Charles Leclerc, who ended up fourth for Ferrari, yet to stop.

That proved the defining moment, with the remainder of the afternoon effectively a high-speed procession to the chequered flag without major incident — despite fears that there could be multiple crashes and red flags as seen in earlier junior races.

Antonelli crossed the line 4.3 seconds clear of Verstappen, with Norris a further 0.7 behind.

Liam Lawson was sixth for Red Bull, with Franco Colapinto seventh for Renault-owned Alpine and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri eighth.

Arvid Lindblad secured precious points for Racing Bulls in their battle for fifth with Alpine, and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg was the final scorer in 10th.

articles.title: Five takeaways from UNC's blowout victory over ETSU in home opener
articles.summary: The Tar Heels wasted no time taking over in their home opener Saturday, dominating ETSU in a 35-3 victory. Here's our top five takeaways from the win.
articles.body:
Saturday was a beautiful day in Chapel Hill...until distant thunderstorms took over in the fourth quarter. Even with an hour-plus weather delay, the North Carolina Tar Heels dominated in their home opener, beating ETSU 35-3.

UNC (2-0) had a scoreless streak spanning back to the first quarter of its season-opening upset of TCU, but Buccaneers (1-2) kicker Ewan Johnson ended that with his 41-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Still, North Carolina held ETSU under 300 yards and forced a pair of turnovers, anchored by two sacks and TFL apiece from Xavier Lewi s and Jaylen Harvey.

The Tar Heels sport an extremely deep running back room. That proved true during Saturday's victory, with six different backs recording a carry. Benjamin Hall led UNC with 49 rushing yards, but 2025 breakout star Demon June stole the show, scoring three touchdowns on just seven carries.

Billy Edwards quickly proved himself as a major quarterback upgrade for North Carolina in Week Zero, consistently moving the football downfield. On Saturday vs. ETSU, Edwards completed 15 of his 20 passes for 244 yards and a pair of touchdowns, finding 11 different pass-catchers.

Big play tight end Jelani Thurman caught four passes for 71 yards and a first-quarter touchdown, opening the Tar Heel scoring attack. Three minutes into the second quarter, Hall hauled in a 26-yard pass on a wheel route, extending UNC's lead to a pair of touchdowns.

As North Carolina prepares for its September 19 ACC opener at Clemson , let's take a deeper dive into five takeaways for Saturday's blowout win over the Bucs:

The Tar Heels' balanced offense can be a weapon going forward

UNC took full advantage of playing an FCS school on Saturday, overwhelming the ETSU defense through the air and on the ground.

North Carolina totaled 427 yards of offense. Edwards and backup QB Miles O'Neill combined for 266 passing yards, then the Tar Heels' ballcarriers totaled 161 yards.

UNC may not have the opportunity to play deep into its depth chart going forward, as the ACC provides a much higher level of competition. North Carolina showed on Saturday, though, that they can beat you any way offensively.

In Week Zero, the Tar Heels held a typically-explosive TCU offense to 10 point and under 300 yards. On Saturday, UNC limited ETSU to a field goal and held it under 300 yards.

Lewis continued his early campaign for ACC Defensive Player of the Year, registering two sacks and TFLs apiece. Harvey, who transferred over from Penn State during the offseason, also recorded two sacks and TFLs apiece.

In the linebacking corps, Richmond transfer Peyton Seelmann tied for a game-high with 10 total tackles. His seven solo takedowns led all players.

North Carolina will be in for a tougher test at Clemson next weekend, but the Tigers have just 32 points through two games. Defense will continue winning the Tar Heels games this fall.

Offensive consistency allowed UNC to play its game

In years' past, the Tar Heel offense has a tendency to start strong and go cold, or fail to start producing until it's too late.

On Saturday vs. ETSU, North Carolina scored in each of the first three quarters. UNC scored its first touchdown in the opening frame, then added 14 points apiece in the second and third quarters.

The Tar Heels don't have to score multiple touchdowns every quarter, but at the very minimum, consistently putting points on the board will continue winning them games.

It's common to see early-season FBS-FCS matchup, typically providing the FBS squad an easy win and the FCS squad an opportunity to gain exposure and valuable experience.

It's also common to see the FBS teams, like UNC, underestimate their opponents at lower levels of competition. See what happened to the Charlotte 49ers in Week 1, as they lost 43-41 to The Citadel in triple overtime.

The Tar Heels never appeared to play at a slower pace on Saturday, consistently moving the football and rarely allowing big plays from the Buccaneers.

There's a very real chance North Carolina can be an ACC dark horse

Two wins. Two games. Once against a preseason Big 12 contender, the other against an ETSU squad with winning records in each of the past two seasons.

UNC's offense is deep, while defense can lock any team down. The Tar Heels face an extremely tough schedule this fall, continuing with a struggling Clemson squad next weekend, but performances in Weeks 0 and 2 show exactly what this team is capable of.

articles.title: Off-Script Ohio: Recapping the Texas disaster and what comes next
articles.summary: Cole and Joey break down Ohio State’s brutal loss to Texas and what it means for the Buckeyes moving forward.
articles.body:
Episode 33 of Off-Script Ohio is all about the Buckeyes' trip to Austin and the aftermath of a brutal loss to Texas. Cole and Joey break down what went right for Ohio State, which players stood out and how the Buckeyes managed to let a game slip away after controlling so much of it.

The second-half collapse is a major focus, including the miscues that allowed Texas to completely flip the game and turn what looked like a comfortable Ohio State victory into a disaster. The guys also look beyond Jeremiah Smith and discuss whether Ohio State's other wide receivers did enough to establish themselves as reliable options in the passing game.

On the other side of the ball, Cole and Joey break down the defense and what the performance means for a unit that entered the season with plenty of questions after losing significant production from last year's team.

From there, the conversation gets bigger. Should Ohio State fans reevaluate Ryan Day? What did the game tell us about Arthur Smith's offense? And how should we view Matt Patricia and the direction of the defense moving forward?

Finally, Cole and Joey look ahead to where the Buckeyes go from here and whether the Texas loss changes their expectations for the rest of the 2026 season. After entering the year with national championship expectations, Ohio State now has to figure out what went wrong in Austin, and whether they can fix it before the season gets away from them.

articles.title: 900 runners embrace rainy conditions for 47th annual Elizabeth River Run
articles.summary: PORTSMOUTH, Va. (WAVY) – A rainy start to the day did not stop nearly 1,000 runners from taking over Portsmouth on Sunday morning for the 47th annual Elizabe...
articles.body:
PORTSMOUTH, Va. (WAVY) – A rainy start to the day did not stop nearly 1,000 runners from taking over Portsmouth on Sunday morning for the 47th annual Elizabeth River Run 10K.

Runners of all ages crossed the finish line near the Portsmouth Pavilion, greeted by crowds of cheering supporters.

10 On Your Side caught up with several runners, including Melanie Hennis and Jim Duffy, who, at age 74, completed not just the 10K but a half marathon on Saturday!

The hot, humid, and rainy conditions added an extra challenge along the course, but some enjoyed the rain.

"It was really hot and humid, but the support was great," Hennis said. "You know, you just got to embrace the suck… I mean, you can't outrun the rain!"

Many of the participants are members of the Tidewater Striders , the local running club that puts on the longstanding tradition. In addition to the main 10K event, the day featured the Crawford Street 1-Mile run for younger participants.

"So we had the mile for the kids, the Crawford Street Mile," said Thomas Hicks, president of Tidewater Striders and race director for the Elizabeth River Run. "And then we had the 10K," he explained. "This is a very competitive race, one of the most competitive races in Virginia."

The event, which drew about 900 runners, also served as a fundraiser benefiting the Children's Museum of Virginia.

"They're letting us use the city, so we wanted to get back to the city," Hicks said. "So we're giving a nice donation, funds that we raised for the race, to the Portsmouth Museum Foundation."

As for Duffy and Hennis, they encourage others to try running.

"You're never too old to start," Duffy said. "Yeah, you're never too old to start," Hennis added. "You can start walking, and then from walking, you start running…"

articles.title: Diamondbacks cut former All-Star with .210 batting average
articles.summary: The 32-year-old had an option clause in his contract for 2027.
articles.body:
The Arizona Diamondbacks designated outfielder Lourdes Gurriel Jr. for assignment on Sunday, Sept. 13. An All-Star in 2023, Gurriel had played only 51 games this season, slashing .210/.254/.290 — all career-lows.

The Diamondbacks held a team option on Gurriel, 32, for the 2027 season.

In effect, they're giving him advance notice of their intention not to bring him back with less than three weeks to go in MLB 's regular season.

In a corresponding move, the Dbacks added designated hitter José Fernández to their roster Sunday.

Gurriel began the season on the injured list after undergoing right ACL surgery in September 2025. His season was a series of stops and starts.

In May, he strained his left hamstring. In July, he strained his right adductor. When Gurriel returned from that IL stint on Sept. 1, he went 3-for-12 (.250) in four games.

Ostensibly the Diamondbacks were more comfortable eating the prorated portion of Gurriel's 2026 salary (and his $5 million buyout clause) than keeping him in the lineup with a wild-card berth at stake.

The San Diego Padres (80-68) have won five straight games to take a 1.5-game lead on the Diamondbacks (79-70) in the race for the NL's final wild-card berth.

The Dbacks host the Texas Rangers later in the day Sunday.

Fernandez, a 22-year-old rookie, slashed .262/.305/.356 in 65 games this season before he was optioned to Triple-A Reno on Aug. 31.

Gurriel is a veteran of nine MLB seasons with the Toronto Blue Jays (2018-22) and Diamondbacks (2023-26). He's a career .271/.316/.445 hitter with 131 home runs and 513 RBIs.

articles.summary: Ryan Garcia sets his eyes on Teofimo Lopez's WBA welterweight title after his TKO win over Conor Benn.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS – Ryan Garcia wants to add another world title to his record, and he's got his eyes on a specific one.

Garcia (25-2, 20 KOs) called for a title unification bout against WBA welterweight champion Teofimo Lopez following his win over Conor Benn this past Saturday at the T-Mobile Arena. Garcia made his first title defense of the WBC welterweight belt, making quick work of Benn (25-1, 14-KOs) with a second-round TKO stoppage. Garcia seems to have a wide range of options, but the fight with Lopez stands out more than any other.

"I want to unify against Teofimo," Garcia told reporters at a post-fight press conference. "I think that's the move. It's a huge fight. Teo is an entertaining dude, and it's going to be one hell of a buildup. He's a good fighter, too. Let's run it."

Lopez won the WBA welterweight title last month, defeating then-champion Rolly Romero, who had taken the WBA title from Garcia in a big upset back in 2025.

Garcia impressed many with his showing on Saturday. Many thought that Benn could push him and give him a tough outing, given his grinding fighting style. However, that was not the case.

"I think that it kind of went exactly how I imagined it," Garcia said. "He was going to decide to put pressure on me right away, kind of banking on the idea that I may start folding somehow and just maybe get tired, but you can't jump in like that. It's just not the move."

Garcia and Benn had a lot to say before the fight, and there was plenty of heat between them. They seemed to have settled their differences in the ring after the fight. All trash talk aside, Garcia thought Benn wasn't at his level, and he felt he proved that on Saturday.

"He's exactly what I thought he was, and he just needs to gain a little bit more experience," Garcia said. "I don't think he has enough experience at this point. I just don't think he was as experienced as me, but I think he will be back, and he went in and tried to fight me."
authors: Danny Segura and Ken Hathaway, MMA Junkie

articles.title: Ronaldo calls for life bans of Saudi Pro League fans after Jota chants
articles.summary: Fans at Al-Taawoun and Al-Hilal game seem to taunt Ruben Neves by chanting name of deceased teammate, Diogo Jota.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo ‌has said that fans who appeared to make chants referencing ⁠former teammate Diogo ⁠Jota at Ruben Neves during a Saudi Pro League match should be banned from football stadiums for life.

The chants occurred on Saturday during ⁠a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves’s side Al-Hilal in Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.

Jota died on July 3, 2025, in a car crash in Zamora, northwestern Spain, along ⁠with his brother Andre Silva. A close friend of Jota, Neves was a pallbearer at his funeral.

Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting “Jota”.

The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who ‌pointed to his eye and then up to the sky in response.

Passing through the mixed zone after the game, Neves commented, “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”

In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account.

“The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” said Ronaldo.

“This is no longer football, and there have to ⁠be limits. People who behave like this should never be ⁠allowed to enter a stadium again.”

The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.

Al-Hilal Club Company announced in a statement on their website on Sunday that they ⁠had filed a complaint with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation relating to the incident. The Saudi Pro League club said they ⁠were “confident” that measures would be taken to “protect the integrity ⁠of sporting competition from offensive practices”.

“The Company expressed its absolute rejection of such actions targeting players or their families, or intended to cause personal offence,” said Al-Hilal’s statement.

Later on Sunday, Al-Taawoun also released ‌a statement regarding the incident, which strongly condemned the offensive chants.

“Such conduct is completely unacceptable and does not represent Al-Taawoun, its supporters or the values for which ‌its ‌terraces are known.”

Al-Taawoun say they will “take all necessary measures in coordination with the relevant authorities to prevent a recurrence and hold offenders accountable”.

articles.title: Kevin Stefanski comments on Falcons' loss to Pittsburgh Steelers
articles.summary: Kevin Stefanski comments on Falcons' loss to Pittsburgh Steelers
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons kept things interesting for most of Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, but they couldn't get the job done. Quarterback Cooper Rush threw two interceptions, including a pick-six.

The Falcons missed two key field goals and committed nine penalties. Head coach Kevin Stefanski addressed the media following the team's Week 1 road loss in Pittsburgh and was quick to point out these issues.

"If you look at the penalties, the turnovers... It's just hard to win on the road when you do those things," said Stefanski. "Those are the things we feel like we can learn from."

Watch Stefanski's full post-game press conference below, as shared by the team's YouTube channel.

The Falcons will return home for a NFC South showdown against the Carolina Panthers in Week 2. Check back Monday for more injury updates.

articles.title: Jerry Jeudy has mediocre line in Week 1
articles.summary: Veteran Jerry Jeudy was nearly non-existent in Week 1
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy posted just two receptions for 26 yards on four targets in Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Huddle Up: Jeudy was previously the unquestioned No. 1 receiver in Cleveland, but 2026 draft picks Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion outproduced him in Game 1, and Harold Fannin Jr. is also a threat to his role in the offense. Jeudy remains more of a low-end WR4 or flex fantasy option in most leagues of 12 or more teams heading into Week 2 at Tampa Bay.
